name: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
role: Educationist and social reformer of the Bengal Renaissance
contribution: As a Sanskrit scholar, education administrator, and Bengali author, he widened access to vernacular learning, supported girls’ schools, and campaigned for Hindu widow remarriage.
context: In nineteenth-century colonial Bengal, he connected debates over Sanskrit learning, school administration, Bengali textbooks, and social custom. His petitions and scriptural arguments helped make widow remarriage a central reform question in the 1850s.
impact: His education work and public campaign contributed to the passage of the Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act in 1856, while his textbooks and school initiatives shaped Bengali education and later discussions of social reform.
highlight: A nineteenth-century Bengali educator and reformer whose work joined school expansion with the campaign for widow remarriage.
seoTitle: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar: Educationist and Social Reformer
seoDescription: Explore Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s role in Bengali education, girls’ schooling, and the campaign that led to the 1856 Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act.
shortAnswer: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a nineteenth-century Bengali educator and social reformer associated with girls’ education and widow-remarriage reform.
